notes: Box score from the Washington Wizards' 98–94 road win over the Chicago Bulls on Nov 20, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via Fox Sports and ABC News), the Chicago Tribune and Roundtable (both via Yahoo Sports), the Chicago Sun-Times, OnTap Sports Net, Bulls On SI, ClutchPoints (via Yahoo Sports) and Fanrecap. All 98 Washington points and all 94 Chicago points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (22–30–23–23 to 29–31–9–25) add up to both totals: 60–52 Chicago at the half and 75–69 Washington after three (AP; OnTap). Team totals (field goals 40 of 90 to 36 of 88, threes 9 of 26 to 9 of 33, free throws 9 of 17 to 13 of 16, rebounds 46–42, points in the paint 54–48, fast-break points 24–4) and the biggest leads (Washington 11, Chicago 15) are from the Covers.com box score; OnTap gives the same paint and fast-break numbers and the AP the 15-point Chicago lead. Bench points (12–47) are from Bulls On SI and match the box score. Records are from the game stories (the site's standings were not yet updated when this was built).

Chicago led by 15 in the second quarter (AP). Washington opened the third on a 15–2 run, and Trae Young's 3-pointer put the Wizards ahead 61–60 (AP; Roundtable). Chicago missed its first 15 shots of the third and shot 3 of 25 in the quarter (OnTap; Bulls On SI; AP), its lowest-scoring quarter of the season (Bulls On SI). Chicago went up 78–77 early in the fourth on a Nic Claxton three-point play (OnTap), and Washington answered with 12 straight points, ending with AJ Dybantsa's layup at 7:31 for 89–78 (AP; OnTap). Claxton's two free throws with 43 seconds left made it 96–94 (AP), Norman Powell missed a tying floater (AP; Chicago Tribune; Sun-Times), and Young's two free throws with 3.4 seconds left made it 98–94 (ClutchPoints; Fanrecap). Anthony Davis had 36 points and 11 rebounds (AP) and went 12 of 13 at the rim (Bulls On SI). Washington has won two straight after an eight-game losing streak (AP) and also won the first meeting, 124–120 in Chicago on Oct 24 (AP; StatMuse). The Wizards host Orlando on Sunday and the Bulls host Denver on Sunday (Plain Text Sports schedule; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of AJ Dybantsa's layup with 7:31 left that made it 89–78 (the AP gives the clock, the layup and the score; OnTap gives Chicago's 78–77 lead before Washington's 12–0 run, so the score before the layup was 87–78). The stories don't describe the move further or name an assist, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Washington Wizards or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to AJ Dybantsa's listed 6-foot-9 and 210 pounds with No. 4 (RealGM; Wikipedia); no wingspan from a sourced measurement was found, so his arms use the standard proportion. He is drawn in Washington's road blue with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
